1 Date of Judgment : 24.03.2025  BRIEF FACTS :-
1.

It is the case of the prosecution that during the period between May 2007 to 18.08.2012 deceased Rajubai was subjected to cruelty on account of demand for dowry by the accused persons that is her husband i.e. accused Paan Singh, her father-in-law i.e. accused Prabhu Dayal and maternal uncle of accused Paan Singh i.e. accused Ram Narayan.
It is also alleged that they committed dowry death of the said deceased Rajubai.
Consequently, charge-sheet for the offence U/s 304B/498A/34 IPC was filed against accused persons.
After the compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C, matter was committed to the Court of Sessions on 05.03.2013.

Charge:-
2. On the basis of material placed on record, vide order dated 08.07.2013 passed by Ld. Predecessor, charge for the offence u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC was framed against the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

PS Ambedkar Nagar Prosecution Evidence :-
3.

In order to bring home the guilt of accused persons, prosecution had examined (22) twenty two witnesses in the prosecution evidence i.e. PW1 SI Krishan Kumar,
PW2 Narayan Singh, PW3 Bunty Rawat (brother), PW4 WSI Praveen, PW5 Bahadur Singh, PW6 Babu Rawat, PW7 Paras Ram, PW8 Smt. Bhagitri, PW9 Pawan Singh,
PW10 Bahadur Singh, PW11 Ct. Mahesh, PW12 Suresh Chand, PW13 Suraj Bhan,
PW14 Rajeev Shukla, PW15 Dr. Sarvesh Tando, PW16 Surender Kumar, PW17 Amit Kumar Sharma, PW18 Dr. Sandeep Sharma, PW19 Insp. Mahesh Kumar, PW20 SI Mam Chand, PW21 SI Anand Kumar Jha, PW22 ACP (Retd) Sunil Kumar Sharma.

Summary of prosecution evidence :-
4. PW2 Narayan Singh (Father of deceased) :- He deposed that deceased Raju Bai was married to accused Paan Singh in June 2007 and he was working as School Teacher in Delhi.
He further testified that he had spent about Rs.4,00,000/- (Four Lakhs) in the marriage of his deceased daughter Raju Bai.
As per his testimony, after about 5-6 months of the said marriage, accused Paan Singh started raising demand of one Bolero Jeep and Rs.1 lac.
PW2 Narayan Singh, however, refused to fulfill the said demand as he was not in a position to give a Bolero Jeep and Rs. 1 Lac.

He further testified that he told accused Paan Singh that when he would be able to make arrangement, he would fulfill the State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
2 said demand.
However, behavior of accused Paan Singh remained adamant.
PS Ambedkar Nagar 5.

As per his testimony, after about two months of the said demand of accused Paan Singh, he called accused Paan Singh's Mama i.e. accused Ram Narayan, their relatives and 'Sarpanch Babu' and they all assembled in a Dharam Shala near Congress Office, Sabalgarh.

He further deposed that after about two days of the said Panchayat, he purchased one motorcycle in the name of his son Bunty and the same was given to accused Paan Singh alongwith Rs. 2 Lakhs in cash.

As per his testimony,
after about two months of giving the said motorcycle and Rs.2 lacs, accused Paan Singh again raised demand of Rs. 15 Lacs cash and also warned him that if his demand was not fulfilled, he would marry one 'Laxmi', who was working in Police Department (Madhya Pradesh).
However, PW2 Narayan refused to fulfill the said demand of Rs. 15 Lacs.

6. PW2 Narayan Singh further testified that on 18 th of last year, (month he did not remember) his daughter Rajubai called his son Bunty and told him that accused Prabhu Dayal (father in law), Paan Singh (husband) and Ram Narayan (Mama) were threatening to kill her and that they were present in Delhi.

He further stated that she also told him that, if PW2 Narayan would not give Rs 15 Lacs,
then they would kill her and marry Laxmi.

He further stated that on the next morning at about 06 AM, his brother in law Suresh received a telephonic call from the neighbour of accused Paan Singh,
who informed him that his daughter had died.
He reached Delhi and went to Police Station.
SDM recorded his statement vide Ex. PW2/A.

He also identified the deadbody of his daughter vide Ex.
PW2/B.

After the postmortem, he received the dead body of his daughter vide receipt Ex. PW2/C.
PS Ambedkar Nagar 7.
During his cross-examination
, PW2 Narayan deposed that deceased Rajubai was around 18 years of age at the time of her marriage and was around 21 years at the time of 'Gauna'.
He affirmed that 'gauna' was the ceremony organized at the time when the girl went to live with her husband and in laws for the first time after marriage.
He further testified that his daughter was being harassed by her husband and in-laws immediately after marriage.
He further stated that only one complaint was lodged by them regarding harassment, however, he could not tell the date or the year of lodging of the same.

8. PW2 Narayan denied the suggestion that on the night before the incident, the deceased had made no complaint of harassment of dowry or that he had not given Rs. 2 Lakhs or a motorcycle to the husband of deceased.
He affirmed that his daughter was very upset regarding the fact that her husband (accused Paan Singh) used to speak to one girl called Laxmi.
He further stated that his daughter had complained about the same to him many times.
He, however, did not know whether accused Paan Singh had an affair with Laxmi or not.
He denied the suggestion that his daughter had committed suicide because of her troubled relationship with her husband (accused) and due to his suspected affair with the girl namely 'Lakshmi'.

9. PW3 Sh.Bunty Rawat (Brother of deceased) :- He deposed that Rajubai (deceased) was married in June, 2007 with accused Paan Singh and after the said marriage, his sister stayed at her parents State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
3 house for three year.
As per his testimony, 'gona' took place in the year 2010, after which she started residing at Village Devri at her in-laws house.

He further testified that after about 4-5 months of her 'gona', accused Ram Narayan (maternal uncle of accused Paan Singh), Ramesh (uncle of accused Paan Singh), accused Prabhu (father of PS Ambedkar Nagar accused Paan Singh) and accused Paan Singh made demand of Rs.1 lac cash and a Bolero Jeep car, however, his father showed their inability to fulfill their demand.

10. As per his testimony, within one-two days, they called a gathering and assembled their relatives including Babu Sarpanch, Sugalli (his father-in-law), accused Ram Narayan (maternal uncle of accused Paan Singh), Ramesh (uncle of accused Paan Singh),
accused Prabhu (father of accused Paan Singh) and accused Paan Singh at Sabal Garh in a Dharamshala near Congress Office

. He further stated that they made request with folded hands to accused persons to keep Rajubai (deceased) peacefully and not to disturb them and that they were not in a position to give car and money, but they agreed to give Rs. 2 Lacs and a Hero Honda CD Deluxe Motorcycle to accused Paan Singh.
He further stated that accused Ram Narayan assured them that henceforth accused Paan Singh would not cause any harassment to his sister.

11. PW3 Bunty further testified that after about two days of the said Panchayat, Rs. 2 Lacs cash and one motorcycle CD Deluxe, Hero Honda was given to accused Paan Singh in his presence as well as in the presence of accused Ram Narayan and Sugalli, Babu Sarpanch and his father.
He further stated that he had bought the said motorcycle in his name on installment basis and the same was handed over to accused Paan Singh.

He further stated that he alongwith Ramesh (uncle of accused Paan Singh) brought Rajubai (deceased) to Delhi at Dakshin Puri, (tenanted accommodation),
where accused Paan Singh was residing and when he reached at his village Andhupura, he received a telephonic call of his sister Rajubai on the same day in the evening and she informed him that she was being beaten up by her husband i.e. accused Paan PS Ambedkar Nagar Singh and and he was asking her as to why she had come.
Thereafter, PW3 Bunty made a telephonic call to accused Paan Singh and asked him as to why he was troubling his sister Rajubai (deceased).
As per the testimony of PW3 Bunty accused Paan Singh told him to take away Rajubai (deceased) as accused Paan Singh did not want her.
12. PW3 Bunty, therefore, came to Delhi and took away Rajubai (deceased) to the Village Andhupura.

After about 15 days, accused Paan Singh alongwith Sh.Radhey Shayam (son of one of Mama of accused Paan Singh) came to their house to take away his sister Rajubai (deceased),
however, they did not send (deceased) Rajubai with accused persons.

PW3 Bunty further stated that in July, 2012 accused Paan Singh went to their house and he took away his sister Rajubai (deceased)
to Delhi.

13. He further stated that on 18.08.2012, he received a telephonic call of his sister Rajubai (deceased), at that time she was weeping and she asked him to take her away as her husband was beating her and he was demanding more money.

As per his testimony, deceased also told him that accused Ram Narayan, Ramesh and Prabhu were also present with them at Delhi and that she asked PW3 Bunty to take her away otherwise the accused persons would kill her.

She, however, also asked PW3 Bunty not to send his brother Suraj Bhan, as he was not aware about the routes and address of State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
4 her residence.

He further testified that on the same day i.e. in the intervening night of 18/19.08.2012, his maternal uncle Suresh Chand informed him about the death of his sister Rajubai,
who in turn was informed by some neighbour known to him.
Thereafter, PW3 Bunty came to Delhi and found that Rajubai was dead.
SDM recorded his statement PS Ambedkar Nagar vide Ex.PW3/A and after postmortem, the dead body of his sister was handed over to him.

14. PW3 Bunty further deposed that his deceased sister had also told him that accused Paan Singh was having illicit relation with some other girl namely Laxmi resident of Gwalior, MP and whenever his sister used to object to the same, accused Paan Singh used to beat her.
15.During his cross-examination

, PW3 Bunty affirmed that they had organized 'gauna' ceremony of his sister Raju bhai (deceased) in the year 2010, however, he did not remember the month of the same but he stated that it was around Holi, in the summer season.
He further testified that a motorcycle was given after four-five months of the said 'gouna' ceremony to accused Paan Singh around the month of July.
He further stated that the said motorcycle was purchased after 2-3 days of the demand, which was made by accused Paan Singh.
He also produced the coloured copy of the RC of the said motorcycle vide Ex. PW3/DA and stated that the original RC was in the possession of accused Paan Singh.
He denied the suggestion that the said motorcycle was purchased for his own use and that the same was never handed over to accused Paan Singh.

He also denied the suggestion that on the day of the incident, accused Ram Narain, Prabhu Dayal or any other relative were not present in Delhi or that they were present in their village at Madhya Pradesh on 18.08.2012 or that he had talked to them on that day.
He also denied the suggestion that he had made a phone call to accused Ram Narain at 07:09 PM on 18.08.2012 or that he had made a phone to accused Ram Narain at 05:30 AM on 19.08.2012.
PS Ambedkar Nagar 16.
He further testified that he had called accused Ram Narain on 19.08.2012 at about 07 AM after taking his number from one Kedar.
He also denied the suggestion that his maternal uncle Vimal had accompanied accused Ram Narain and Prabhu Dayal and other persons in the car to Delhi.
He also denied that his sister had committed suicide because that accused Paan Singh was having an affair with another woman namely Laxmi.
Sh .Paras Ram (uncle of deceased) :- He also testified on the same lines as the aforesaid witness.
He deposed that after the solemnization of marriage of deceased Rajubai, her in-laws of started demanding money i.e. Rs. 2 Lakhs and Bolero car.
He further testified that accused had also threatened that in case their demand of Rs. 2 Lakhs and Bolero car was not met, they would kill Rajubai.

He further stated that accused Ramesh, Paan Singh, Prabhu, accused Manisha (Nanad)
(discharged), Sheela (mother in law) (discharged), maternal uncle Ram Narayan were demanding Rs. 2 Lakhs and the Bolero car and all these persons had killed his niece.
18.As per the testimony of PW7 Paras, on 18 th his nephew Suraj Bhan had received a phone call of his niece Rajubhai that the accused persons had threatened to kill her in case Rs. 2 Lakhs and one Bolero car were not given to them.

He further stated that probably, on 19 th information regarding State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/

19.In his cross
- examination
, he deposed that he was aware of the dispute between accused Paan Singh and the deceased, on account of accused Paan Singh having an affair with a girl namely Lakshmi.
He denied the suggestion that he was deposing falsely or that no dowry was ever demanded by accused persons or by anyone in their family.
He further denied that the deceased had committed suicide due to extra marital affair of accused Paan Singh with Laxmi.
20.PW8 Smt. Bhagitri (Mother) :- She also deposed on the same lines as the aforesaid witness.

She also deposed that at the time of marriage of her daughter Rajubai with accused Paan Singh, they had given Rs.4 Lakhs in cash in addition to 2 'Tolas' jewellery and other household articles i.e. TV,
fridge, double bed, cooler, almirah, all set of utensils, the sets of clothes, almost all the articles which are required in a home.

She further stated that after about one year of the said marriage, the in-laws of her daughter started harassing her on the pretext that she had brought less dowry in marriage and were demanding more dowry i.e. Rs. 2 Lakhs, 2 Tolas gold and one motorcycle.
21.As per her testimony
, they had met the said demand and accordingly, Rs. 2 Lakhs, 2 Tolas gold as well as motorcycle were handed over to the accused persons after one year of the marriage.

She further stated that pursuant to handing over the said cash, gold and motorcycle, accused Paan Singh had come to their place for taking her daughter back to matrimonial home and she had sent her daughter with accused Paan Singh and for about one year, her daughter was treated well by accused persons.
Thereafter, accused persons again started harassing her.

Her daughter Rajubai told her that there was a girl PS Ambedkar Nagar namely Lakshmi who was in the police, who was instigating accused Paan Singh to eliminate Rajubai and to marry her (Laxmi).
22.During her cross-examination
, PW8 Smt. Bhagitri was confronted with her statement u/s 161 CrPC where the name of Laxmi was not mentioned.
As per her testimony, the 'gouna' ceremony of her deceased daughter Raju Bai was performed simultaneously with her marriage and at that time her son Bunty, her husband Narain were present.
She denied the suggestion that her daughter's 'gauna' was performed after 3 year of her marriage.

23.She, however, stated that accused persons namely Prabhu (father in law), Ramesh (Uncle of Paan Singh), Ram Narayan (Maternal uncle of the accused Paan Singh), accused Paan Singh (husband),
Manisha (Nanad), Radhey Shyam (cousin devar), Sushila (mother in law) and Umedi (Bua Saas)
had a meeting in which they had decided to eliminate Rajubai (deceased) and at the same time, one Lakshmi with whom accused Paan Singh had an extra marital affair, offered that she would persuade her parents to give Rs.15 Lakhs, if accused Paan Singh married her.
24.PW10 Bahadur Singh (tenant) :- He testified that he and accused Paan Singh were tenants in premises L-197, Dakshinpuri, New Delhi.
He testified that accused Paan Singh used to reside at first floor whereas he was residing on the third floor of the aforesaid premises.
He further testified that the wife of accused Paan Singh i.e. Rajubai often used to speak to her brother and other family members from his mobile phone.

He further testified that on 18.08.2012 and 19.08.2012, deceased State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
6 Rajubai had spoken to her parents from his mobile phone and the number of his mobile phone was 9560129376.
PS
Ambedkar Nagar 25.During his cross-examination
, he affirmed that on 18.08.2012 and 19.08.2012, neither accused Ram Narayan nor Prabhu or any other relative had come to the said premises.
He further deposed that accused persons Ram Narayan and Prabhu had come along with the family members of the deceased after the information of her death was given to them.
He also affirmed that accused Paan Singh was suffering from Hepatitis B and was being treated for the same.

He further affirmed that deceased Raju bai often used to complain that accused Paan Singh was having relations with a girl and that he used to talk with her on the phone, due to which they used to have quarrels.

He,
however, stated that deceased Rajubai never told them about any harassment being meted out to her on account of dowry demand.
26.PW12 Suresh Chand :- He deposed that the marriage of his niece Rajubai was solemnized with accused Paan Singh in year 2007 and on 19.08.2012, he came to know about the death of his niece.

He further testified that he alongwith other relatives came to Delhi and had given a handwritten complaint to SDM, Hauz Khas and the same was placed on record vide Ex.PW12/A and he had also given a similar complaint to police vide Ex.PW12/B.
He had also given a complaint to the SDM to verify the caste of accused Paan Singh as he had claimed to be a scheduled tribe and had got work on that ground.

The said complaint was placed on record vide Ex.PW12/C.
27.As per his testimony

, in his complaint, he had stated that on 18.08.2012 at about 7.00 p.m., he had received a phone call from mobile no.9560129376 on his mobile no.982625410 and the caller Rajubai had informed him that accused persons Prabhu, Ramesh, Paan Singh, accused persons Sheela, Manisha (discharged), Ram Narayan, Radhey Shyam, Rambir, Rajender, Bahadur and PS Ambedkar Nagar Bunty had surrounded her in a room and were compelling her to demand Rs.1 lakhs and one Bolero vehicle, otherwise, she would be killed.

They had also compelled Rajubai (deceased) to convey to them that in case they failed to meet their demands, accused Paan Singh would marry Lakshmi, whose parents were offering Rs.15,00,000/- to accused Paan Singh.
28. During his cross-examination conducted by Ld defence counsel
, he deposed that he knew accused Ram Narayan since 2007.
However, he stated that he did not call accused Ram Narayan to ensure about the well being of Rajubai (deceased).
As per his testimony, one Kedar, Ex Surpanch had called him and informed him about death of deceased Raju Bai and that accused Ram Narayan was with him at that time.

Defence Evidence :-
32. DW-1 Dr. (Col.) S.K. Thakur :-

He had testified that as per his prescription dated 22.11.2011 of accused Paan Singh placed on record as Ex. DW1/B, he had mentioned that accused Paan Singh was suffering from Hepatitis B viral infection as on 22.11.2011.

He also testified that as per his prescription dated 18.06.2012 of accused Paan Singh placed on record as Ex. DW1/C, the said accused was coming to him regularly for checkup in relation to Hepatitis B viral infection.

He further testified that normally, the other partner should also receive Hepatitis B vaccination and till such time the said vaccination is not taken, the said person should avoid physical relation or use protection.
33.
During his cross-examination conducted by Ld. Addl. PP for State
, he affirmed that there was no mention in the said prescriptions of any such advice being given to accused Paan Singh that he should not have sexual relationship.
34. DW3 Pritam Singh :- He deposed that he knew accused Paan Singh as he belonged to the same village.
He further testified that he was a Sarpanch of the village from 2010 to 2015.

As per his testimony, he came to know about the death of deceased Rajubai in the morning of 19.08.2012 and on 19.08.2012, PS Ambedkar Nagar Ramesh (chacha of accused Paan Singh) came to his house and requested him to lend his Mahindra Bolero car bearing registration number MP06-A-2313, as the family members of accused Paan Singh wanted to go to Delhi.

He placed on record the original receipt from NHAI Toll Plaza at Mahuvan vide Ex. DW3/A,

40. DW6 Ajay Singh Meena (brother of accused Paan Singh) :- He testified that at the time of incident, he was living with his brother i.e. accused Paan Singh at L-block, Dakshinpuri.
He further testified that in the intervening night of 18/19.08.2012, he was at home when the alleged incident occurred.
He further testified that on that day, he was with his brother and sister in law i.e. accused Paan Singh and deceased Rajubai at night and no one else was there in the house.
As per his testimony, he did not go to school on that day as he was sick.

He further stated that his brother i.e.
accused Paan Singh had gone to school in the morning and he came back from school around 02 PM, after which an PS Ambedkar Nagar argument took place between his brother and sister in law i.e. deceased Rajubai between 03 PM to 04 PM.
He further stated that his brother was talking to someone over the phone and his sister-in-law thought that he was talking to Laxmi.
She further stated that his sister-in-law got upset over the same and vented her anger on his brother.
He further stated that accused Paan Singh also argued with his wife i.e. deceased Rajubai and told her that he was not talking to Laxmi.
He further stated that at night he had fever and was not able to sleep properly.
Therefore, he woke up his sister-in-law around 12 AM and told her that he had stomach ache.

He further stated that deceased Rajubai told him to call his brother i.e. Paan Singh and to ask State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
9 him to take care of him, while she went to the outer room to sleep.
He further stated that accused Paan Singh came and slept next to him in a room and after about 2-3 hours, he heard a loud noise from the outer room.
He further stated that he and his brother i.e. accused Paan Singh went outside and saw that deceased Rajubai had hung herself from a ceiling fan with her saree and a shoe rack had fallen down.

41. During his cross-examination conducted by Ld. Addl. PP for the State, he denied the suggestion that he was not in Delhi on the day of incident and that is why his statement was not recorded by the police.
He further denied the suggestion that his bhabhi i.e. deceased had committed suicide due to the illicit relationship of accused Paan Singh with one Laxmi.
He also denied the suggestion that accused Prabhu Dayal and Ram Narayan had demanded money from the parents of the deceased.
42. Thereafter, Defence Evidence was closed vide order dated 05.10.2024.

PS Ambedkar Nagar Appreciation of Evidence and Findings :-
43.

It is the case of the prosecution that during the subsistence of marriage of deceased Rajubai with accused Paan Singh, she was subjected to cruelty on account of demand for dowry by the said accused as well as her father-in-law i.e. Prabhu Dayal and maternal uncle of accused Paan Singh i.e.
Ram Narayan.
It had also been alleged that on 18.08.2012, the said accused persons committed dowry death of deceased Rajubai at L-197, Dakshinpuri, Ambedkar Nagar, New Delhi.

44. It is well settled that in Kaliyaperumal and Anr Vs State of Tamil Nadu, CrL.
1358 of 2002, Hon'ble Supreme Court had held that :-
In order to attract section 304B IPC, the essential ingredients are as follows:-
1. The death of a woman should be caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under a normal circumstances.
2. Such a death should have occurred within seven years of her marriage.

4. Such cruelty or harassment should be for or in connection with demand of dowry.
5. Such cruelty or harassment is shown to have been meted out to the woman soon before her death.
45. In order to prove the same, prosecution had examined the father of deceased i.e. PW2 Ram Narayan.
He had testified that his deceased daughter was married with accused Paan Singh in June 2007 and at that time accused Paan Singh was working as a teacher in MP.

Thereafter, the word 'deemed' used in that Section is to be read down to require an accused to prove his innocence, but beyond reasonable doubt.
The 'deemed' culpability of the accused leaving no room for the accused to prove innocence was, accordingly, read down to a strong 'presumption' of his culpability.
The accused is required to rebut this presumption by proving his innocence.

In order words, 'shown' will have to be read up to mean 'proved' but only to the extent of preponderance of probability.
Thereafter, the word 'deemed' used in that Section is to be read down to require an accused to prove his innocence, but beyond reasonable doubt.
The 'deemed' culpability of the accused leaving no room for the accused to prove innocence was, accordingly, read down to a strong 'presumption' of his culpability.
The accused is required to rebut this presumption by proving his innocence.
The same view was reiterated in Ramakant Mishra @ Lalu etc Vs State of UP, 2015 (3)
SCALE 186. '
State vs Paan Singh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166260270/
16 74.
Be that as it may, the prosecution has duly established that the deceased was subjected to cruelty by accused Paan Singh 'soon before her death' on account of demand for dowry, due to which she was driven to commit suicide.
The evidence led by accused was not found to be cogent and reliable and the accused failed to rebutt the presumption under section 113B Indian Evidence Act raised against him.
In view of the aforesaid facts, the prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubt against accused Paan Singh and accused Prabhu Dayal and Ram Narayan.

It had been argued that the said testimony is in contradiction with the testimony of mother of deceased i.e. PW8 Bhagitri, where by she had deposed that the 'gauna' ceremony was performed simultaneously with the marriage.
Even otherwise, the factum that the death of the deceased took place within seven years of her marriage to the accused is not belied by the factum of gauna ceremony being held at the same time of marriage or after marriage of the deceased with the accused.

Accused Paan Singh is hereby convicted for the offence u/s 498A/304B IPC and accused Prabhu Dayal and Ram Narayan are convicted for the offence u/s 498A IPC.
